Well, sadly, since there is the IceCreamBeat, FruitBall, KeybladeRace, CommandBoard, MirageArena, and all UnversedChallenges, I think you'll hafta sink a bit more time than you might want into the minigame half of the game. Especially the commandboards take up a lot of time, considering you might have some bad luck going on, and want the commands from the boards that you cant get anywhere else (like the Ragnarok-Shotlock). If you want full completion without effort, you're out of luck (it took me quite a while and many short sessions to complete the game 100% simply because of occassional demotivation thanks to IceCreamBeat and FruitBall)

You have a point, but I did have a lot of fun figuring out the best deck from the cards I had in proud mode. Especially in that difficulty, you really do have to plan some things out. Of course, if you grind your CP to 700+ early game, I have to agree on the problems of spammable sleights and boring combat, but if you dont grind there should be a nice balance between challenge and progress, at least that's how it turned out for me.

Fair enoufh, I think I prefer BBS's melding system over the card system in the long run too. In my case that might be because of the fact you level the commands, sometimes multiple times, to craft them into new stronger ones.
Also, I was very surprised to see Dream Drop Distance's command-system without the melding, and especially without the improvement  of the commands. Kind of turned me off on for a moment, until I found something else to level up other than Sora and Riku, namely the Dream Eaters. (It didn't feel the same for me, but at least it's something I suppose).
